name: flight-to-do-desktop
description: Electron shell for the flight to-do: serves the built renderer and will own the Telegram send.

scripts.start: npm run build && env -u ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE electron .
scripts.//start: Serves the static renderer from front-end/dist — the shape a packaged build runs in.
scripts.dev: npm run build && env -u ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE RENDERER_URL=http://localhost:5173 electron .
scripts.//dev: Loads the Vite dev server for HMR — run `npm run dev:renderer` at the root first.
scripts.//typecheck: esbuild only strips types, so this is the real check.
scripts.//package: Builds the .app/.dmg. The renderer must already be built — use the root `npm run package`, which enforces the order.

//electron: Pinned, not ranged: electron-builder needs an exact version to fetch matching binaries, and runtime upgrades should be deliberate.
//name: Drives app.getName() and so the userData path — keep it aligned with productName in electron-builder.yml, or a packaged build reads a different data directory than a dev one.
author: Mau Ulisse Luz
//electron-run-as-node: VS Code's integrated terminal exports ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 for its own tooling. Inherited here it makes require("electron") return the binary path instead of the API, so app is undefined and main dies on the first call. Unset per-invocation rather than relying on the shell.
